identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is an inspection log for a propane-powered forklift (Toyota 8FGU25, unit FL-2) required by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). Operators inspect the truck before each shift using a 12-point checklist (tires, forks, mast, horn, lights, seat belt, brakes, steering, propane tank, fire extinguisher, data plate, and overhead guard) and record defects if found. The log covers September 1–18, 2026, and is maintained by two certified operators, M. Chen and J. Rivera.
scan.freshness_note: This log is current as of 2026-09-18 (today). It is an ongoing record that should continue to be maintained.

gaps.title: Missing inspections between Sep 2 and Sep 7
gaps.description: The truck's hour meter shows it ran on Sep 3, 4, 5, and 6 (rising from 4,819 to 4,834 hours), but pre-shift inspections were not logged for those days. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) requires examination before each shift; the document itself notes this requirement.
gaps.fix: Inspect the truck on every day it is used and record the results, even for days in the past if the records can be reconstructed. Going forward, ensure the log captures every shift the truck operates.
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Supervisor review signature missing
gaps.description: The log form includes a line for 'Supervisor review:' and 'Date:' but neither is filled in. While the log is being completed by operators, supervisor oversight and sign-off is part of the maintenance record.
gaps.fix: Have the supervisor review the log at regular intervals (weekly or monthly is typical) and sign and date the review line.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) does not explicitly mandate supervisor sign-off, but OSHA expects records to show oversight

gaps.title: Defect resolution not documented
gaps.description: On Sep 9, the horn was found defective ('Horn not working'). The log does not show when the horn was repaired or when the truck was returned to service. OSHA 1910.178(q)(7) states do not use a truck if a defect affects safety.
gaps.fix: Document the date and nature of repairs made. Either add a 'Repairs/Actions' column or add a note in the log when the defect is corrected (for example, 'Sep 10 Horn repaired by maintenance'). Do not resume use until the repair is complete and verified.

scan.confidence_notes: I am confident in the factual content of the log itself—dates, operator names, checklist results, and notes are all clearly recorded. The defect on Sep 9 (horn) is explicitly noted. The gap in inspections Sep 3–6 is clearly visible in the data: the hour meter jumps from 4,819 to 4,834 hours, confirming the truck ran but was not inspected on those days. OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) requirement to inspect before each shift is cited in the document header. I am confident the lack of supervisor sign-off is visible on the form. I am less certain about the intent regarding the Sep 9 horn defect—the log does not state whether the truck was taken out of service or when it was repaired, so I inferred that this should have been documented.
